name: Air-Ship Based High-Altitude Pseudo Satellite (AS-HAPS)
variant: AS-HAPS programme — airship/solar-powered high-altitude pseudo-satellite for long-endurance ISR/comms

header.one_liner: A 2026 Acceptance of Necessity cleared development/procurement of an air-ship-based high-altitude pseudo-satellite (AS-HAPS) — a solar/battery-powered airship loitering in the stratosphere for persistent ISR and communications, filling the gap between UAVs and satellites.
header.maker: Programme — Indian defence R&D/industry (defence/DRDO-linked); collaborating partners to be finalised under the AoN
header.indigenous_label: Emerging Indian development; high-altitude airship/pseudo-satellite technology nascent

what_it_is.prose: The Air-Ship Based High-Altitude Pseudo Satellite (AS-HAPS) is an Indian programme — cleared by an Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) in 2026 — to develop or acquire a high-altitude pseudo-satellite (HAPS). A HAPS is a lighter-than-air or fixed-wing platform that loiters in the stratosphere (roughly 15-25 km altitude), above most weather and below satellites, powered by solar cells or batteries, and capable of very long endurance (days to months). It provides persistent intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR), communications relay, and earth-observation coverage analogous to a satellite but at a fraction of the cost and with rapid, local deployment. The 'air-ship based' variant refers specifically to a lighter-than-air airship or hybrid dirigible design. For India, an AS-HAPS is strategically valuable because it offers persistent, re-locatable ISR and communications over the high-altitude Himalayan border regions (including the contested Line of Actual Control with China), where both satellite revisit and ground infrastructure are limited, and where conventional UAV endurance is insufficient. The 2026 AoN signals a deliberate push to advance the programme from concept to development/procurement. The technology is globally nascent — no nation has fielded a fully operational military HAPS at scale — which makes India's programme both a potential frontrunner and a high technical risk. The platform would sit between the UAV fleet and the satellite constellation in India's ISR/communications architecture.

deployments_procurement.summary: The AS-HAPS received an Acceptance of Necessity in 2026, advancing it from concept into the development/procurement pipeline. Prior small-scale demonstrations of high-altitude airship/pseudo-satellite and solar-HAPS technology in India (defence/DRDO-linked initiatives and industry experiments) provide a limited base. The programme is early-stage: platform selection (lighter-than-air vs hybrid), payload, endurance and budget are being detailed under the AoN.

import_dependencies.summary: As an emerging technology at AoN stage, AS-HAPS dependence is largely on nascent components — solar cells, high-altitude battery/energy storage, lightweight structure composites and stratospheric flight-control — several of which have limited indigenisation.

items.note: Stratospheric endurance depends on advanced solar cells and lightweight batteries — partly imported; indigenisation under way
Ultra-light envelope and structure materials for stratospheric loiter — sourced/experimental
High-altitude flight control, station-keeping and beyond-line-of-sight comms partly imported/custom
EO/IR and radar payloads indigenising (DRDO) but some sensors imported at high performance

faq.question: What is a high-altitude pseudo-satellite (HAPS)?
faq.answer: A HAPS is a platform — in this case an air-ship (lighter-than-air) design — that loiters in the stratosphere (~15-25 km) over many days to months, powered by solar cells or batteries, providing persistent ISR, communications relay and earth-observation analogous to a satellite but cheaper, local and re-deployable.

faq.question: Why does India want an AS-HAPS?
faq.answer: An AS-HAPS provides persistent, re-locatable ISR and communications over the high-altitude Himalayan border regions (Line of Actual Control) where satellite revisit and ground infrastructure are limited and conventional UAV endurance is insufficient.

faq.question: Where does the AS-HAPS programme stand in 2026?
faq.answer: The programme received an Acceptance of Necessity (AoN) in 2026, advancing it from concept into the development/procurement pipeline. It is early-stage: platform type, payload, endurance and budget are being detailed.
